question.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\text{gcd}(321,213)=3$

II. $\text{gcd}(321,213)=1$

III. $321$ and $213$ are coprime

current_example.problem:
Which of the following statements are true?

I. $\textrm{gcd}(651, 574) = 7$

II. $\textrm{gcd}(651, 574) = 1$

III. $651$ and $574$ are coprime
current_example.worked_solution:
Recall that two integers are coprime if their greatest common divisor is $1.$ 

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

- Statement I is true, while statement II is false. Indeed, let's use the Euclidean algorithm, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}651 & = & 574\cdot 1 & + & 77 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 574 & = & 77\cdot 7 & + & 35 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 77 & = & 35\cdot 2 & + & 7 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 35 & = & 7\cdot 5 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

The last positive remainder is ${\color{blue}7}.$ So, the greatest common divisor of $651$ and $574$ is $7\mathbin{:}$

$$
\textrm{gcd}(651, 574) = 7.
$$

- Statement III is false. Since $\textrm{gcd}(651, 574) > 1,$ the numbers are not coprime.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
